content.intro: This lesson covers Secrets During Image Builds. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: Keep deployment configuration separate from image source. Environment files and variable interpolation are convenient for non-secret configuration, but secrets need a controlled delivery mechanism, restricted access, appropriate rotation, and careful handling in logs and build output. Learning secrets during image builds helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Keep deployment configuration separate from image source. items.title: BuildKit secret mounts
items.text: A secret needs a restricted path from its source to the process that needs it. Avoid putting it in images, normal build arguments, source control, or diagnostic output.

Relate the result back to secrets during image builds rather than assuming that a successful command proves the wider system is correct.

items.title: Avoiding secret persistence in image layers
items.text: Image layers are shared read-only filesystem changes; each running container has a writable layer whose contents are not a replacement for persistent storage.

items.title: Restricting access during a build
items.text: Automate the same validated commands that developers can run locally, keep build inputs explicit, and retain test results and release artifact identifiers.

items.title: Reviewing build output and cache behavior
items.text: BuildKit/Buildx can improve parallel work and cache reuse. Confirm builder, target platform, and output mode so a successful build actually produces the artifact you intend.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Secrets During Image Builds
content_blocks.expected_output: The build succeeds only when the secret is supplied and the mounted file is present; the file is not copied into an image layer by this instruction.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Create a temporary secret outside version control and pass it with `docker build --secret id=api_token,src=PATH_TO_LOCAL_SECRET .` after replacing the placeholder path.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Delete the temporary lab secret through your normal secure file-handling process; never paste real credentials into the lesson or commit them.
content_blocks.safety_note: Secret handling example. Do not create or use a real credential for a demo; use a disposable dummy value.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
